title: An SQL query as a text block

blocks.text: Text blocks became standard in Java 15. The page's pitfalls are all about whitespace:

items: The compiler strips the **common leading whitespace** of the content lines and the closing `"""` line, so the closing delimiter's position decides how much indentation is removed. A closing `"""` further left than the content keeps the difference as indentation.
A closing `"""` on its **own line** ends the text with a newline; placing it right after the last content line does not.
A `\` at the end of a line suppresses that line terminator, joining the line to the next **with nothing in between**; any space you want must be written.

blocks.text: Pair a text block with `formatted()` to fill in values. Write the class `Queries` using text blocks:

items: `select(String table)` returns these four lines, each ending with `"\n"`, with no leading spaces:

items.text:
SELECT id, name, email
FROM <table>
WHERE active = true
ORDER BY name ASC

items: `inline(String table)` returns the same query as **one** line, parts separated by single spaces, with no line terminator at all.

rows:
`"SELECT id, name, email
FROM users
WHERE active = true
ORDER BY name ASC
"`
`"SELECT id, name, email FROM orders WHERE active = true ORDER BY name ASC"`

cases.says: select gives the four lines of the query with the table filled in, and inline gives the query on one line.
select is exactly the four lines, each starting at column 0 with none of the source's indentation and no stray whitespace.
select ends with a line terminator after its last line.
inline is exactly one line, with one space between the parts and no final newline.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A closing delimiter on its own line gives the text a final newline, and a trailing backslash removes it.
String.formatted() fills a text block's placeholders as a method chain.
A text block strips the common leading whitespace of its content lines and closing delimiter line, so the closing delimiter's position sets the indentation.
A backslash at the end of a line joins it to the next line with nothing in between.
